reviews.review: One of the best games i've ever played! Super fun, great gameplay, and a cute story. Highly recommended!

I'll be honest, I didn't really get this game the first few times I played it. It seemed interesting with its specific aesthetic (your character being a only handful of pixels tall for one) but a bit too difficult without much of a point. I pushed through this a little bit and found that the gameplay is very rewarding and actually quite fun once you have established yourself in a playthrough with lots of powerups applied. One thing to note is that as you explore through and hit certain milestones you will unlock more powerups, characters, and possible gameplay modifiers. These can serve to make the game a bit more forgiving in some cases and quite a bit more interesting in the rest.

The lore kind of, ahem, coalesces into a narrative as you read bits of text here and there, look though the descriptions of enemies and items, and explore the different environments the game tosses you in. Some of the descriptions leave a sense of uneasiness and sonder, and as a whole you eventually learn why everything attacks you so viciously even though it seems a peaceful approach and coexistence should be possible, or at least would have been at one point.

The pixel art is good by my standards and really helps cement in the idea that your character is a very small part of a pretty large environment with some absolutely massive adversaries by comparison. Everything conforms to a wider aesthetic very well and the game feels very polished despite its simplistic graphics.

[b]The soundtrack is amazing, and I would recommend the game on this basis alone.[/b] Its theming is very on point and the track for the final zone of the game is such a beautiful and eerie piece in my opinion. I would recommend you not spoil yourself with what it sounds like if you plan on playing; working through the gauntlet up until that point and hearing it chime for the first time in was a special experience. The theme for Sky Meadow, Chanson d'Automne is a close second, especially taking into account the lore context of the beings that live there.

Overall, it was a bit difficult to get into at the very beginning but the game has a momentum that carries you deeper in and pushing for higher times, scores, and an understanding of the game's world. Amazing soundtrack and the pixel art is pretty good too.

Heck ya.

This glitchy game has no right being as fun as it is. Stay away from walls when doing teleport shenanigans and you should be fine. Unfortunately mods are not stable, and there is no more developer support on the way. 

Flying enemies are immune to random things for no apparent reason, but it's not a big deal.

One character can kill themselves if they happen to have 1 or 2 items that really benefit them... watch out!
